2026 年 11 月 1 帖

2026-11-01 · 共 2 条 · ♥ 3,390 在 X 上查看 ↗

网红（influencer）受注意力驱动，所以他们的内容必须被优化成“消费完就忘”（廉价多巴胺）。

个人品牌受金钱驱动，所以他们的内容必须被优化成把你一步步推进他们的销售漏斗。

匠人（artisan）受作品质量带来的满足感驱动。他们需要注意力和金钱，但唯一的目的是把更多时间花在自己热爱的工作及其影响上。

成为一名匠人。

EN 原文

An influencer is incentivized by attention, so their content must be optimized to be consumed and forgotten (cheap dopamine).

A personal brand is incentivized by money, so their content must be optimized to move you down their sales funnel.

An artisan is incentivized by the satisfaction that comes from the quality of their work. They need attention and money, but for the sole purpose of spending more time on work they enjoy and the impact it has.

Become an artisan.

如果你很容易对东西上瘾，你就拥有最罕见的特质之一。

大多数人对任何东西的兴趣都维持不了一周以上。你却能不知不觉地在一件事上耗掉 6 个小时。

现在，这份投入流向了游戏、信息流，以及任何最先钩住你的东西。这是唯一的问题。

选一件真正值得上瘾的难事。一项技能、你的身体、你的工作。给它同样的痴迷，坚持 2 年，你就会超过那些已经做了 10 年的人。

EN 原文

If you get addicted to things easily, you have one of the rarest traits there is.

Most people can't stay interested in anything for more than a week. You can lose 6 hours to something without noticing.

Right now that goes to games, feeds, and whatever hooks you first. That's the only problem.

Pick one hard thing actually worth being addicted to. A skill, your body, your work. Give it the same obsession for 2 years and you'll pass people who've been at it for 10.

EN 原文

Find proven topics, save unique ideas, chat with anything, and schedule to all platforms here:
https://eden.so

串内续帖

大多数社交媒体工具都很烂。

（这 7 年做下来，我全都试过了。）

它们声称能帮你爆火。

它们声称你会在社交媒体上快速增长。

它们声称会让你轻松，这样你就能在没有任何技能或理解的情况下涨粉。

而现在它们正试图走向完全智能体化，而这只有在你知道自己在做什么时才有效（这个我们稍后再谈，我们做了社交媒体的 MCP）。

另外，当人人都有优势时，它就不再是优势。

我向你保证，我热爱 AI，但让它替你写所有东西，尤其是作为初学者，等于判了死刑。
你可能会走运，有一条、两条或三条帖子表现不错。

你可能会涨很多粉（因为他们就是用这个承诺让你掏钱的），但然后呢？

你能复制它吗？

你的受众真的在乎你是谁吗？

还是说，你只是又一个昙花一现的人，就像其他所有试图“速成涨粉”的创作者一样？

你喜爱的那些创作者……那些输出真正改变你人生的想法的人，明白当所有人都在争先恐后地输出尽可能多的垃圾内容时，创作过程（捕捉、重新浮现和综合想法）才是你的竞争优势。

所以我们做了一个真正的解决方案。

献给那些内心深处知道“推销给你的玩具和噱头并不是长期策略”的人。

它叫 Eden。创作者的第二大脑。

它拥有其他所有人都有的排程、数据分析、自动私信和爆款研究（覆盖所有平台）功能——由一个知道什么有用、什么没用的人打造。

但它还内置了构思过程，而这个过程是不能跳过的。

下面是它的样子，以及如何写出一条人们真正在乎的帖子：

1）从任何地方保存灵感（并阅读 + 划线）

在智能体或 AI 聊天里捕捉想法、帖子、链接和划线，听起来简直是地狱。

不是所有东西都需要、或者应该被塞进一个聊天界面。

在 Eden 里你可以：

- 粘贴任何社交帖子链接（任何帖子我们都能转录）

- 与 Kindle、Snipd 或 Readwise 集成

- 导入 X 或 Substack 书签

- 随手记下想法，或在文档里写作

- 在阅读模式中打开任何 YouTube 字幕或文章并划线

我们会自动为你的一切分类和打标签，这样我们的 Deep Synthesis（深度综合）智能体就能在你的资料库中发现新颖的联系与关联——让你轻松重新找回那些你以为已经丢失的想法。［原文此处 “idaes” 为 “ideas” 的拼写错误］

2）研究什么有效，学习顶尖创作者

爆款（outlier）工具是每个创作者的基本功。

当你为一个 YouTube 视频做研究时，你会寻找表现出色的标题和缩略图，并研究别人什么做法奏效了。

但其他所有平台呢？

我们拥有一个覆盖所有平台、超过 300 万条帖子且仍在增长的社交语料库。

你可以刷 Discover（发现）页面寻找灵感，搜索任何创作者并按热门帖子筛选，或在 AI 聊天中使用 Deep Social 在所有内容中搜索。

正是这一点让 MCP 能够获取热门话题，而无需你自己抓取数百万条帖子。

3）在一个地方用所有素材创作，建立素材库（swipe files）

我想我永远不会放弃写作。

我喜欢早上坐下来，打开一页，研究好的想法，然后把它变成值得分享的东西。

在 Eden 里，你在 Boards（看板）上工作。

你可以粘贴社交帖子，建立可分享的素材库；也可以添加你的大纲和草稿，同时把你的资料库、聊天或想法打开在旁边。

4）与任何东西聊天，获取你需要的信息

Claude 和 ChatGPT 必不可少，但它们是瞎的。

它们读不了社交链接。它们看不到什么在流行。

当你写脚本、文章、帖子或草稿时——你需要能从你研究的来源中提取信息。在当今世界，这通常意味着社交帖子、YouTube 视频和文章。

5）起草、排程并发布到所有平台

X、Instagram、LinkedIn、Substack、Threads、TikTok 和 YouTube Shorts。

是的，我们是最早支持向 X 和 Substack 定时发布文章的工具之一。

你不必再往每个平台复制粘贴了。

你只需写好、排程，然后让它发到所有平台。

6）或者全部通过 MCP 完成

我不相信内容的未来是完全智能体化的。

但这并不意味着 AI 不能帮忙研究热门帖子、构思和排程内容。

你负责写作和思考，让 AI 处理杂活，以及把你需要找到的想法重新翻出来。

有了 Eden，你不必放弃你的 Claude、Hermes 或其他智能体工作流。你只需连接 MCP，就可以搭建你自己的智能体内容系统——如果你好这口的话。

Eden 就是社交媒体 MCP。

你不必再为抓取工具付费了。

你终于可以获取趋势、任何社交链接和任何账号。

你可以获取你的数据分析，用我们的基础设施搭建内容仪表盘（你不需要把维护它当作一份全职工作），并发布内容。

我们实际上已经做了 4 个技能（skills），用于深度话题研究、个人品牌策略、搭建内容指挥中心等——我们会在下面附上链接。

总而言之：

如果你是创作者，Eden 就是你的大本营。

它是你每天写作、研究和发布的地方。

在下面免费试用：

EN 原文

Most social media tools suck.

(I've tried them all over 7 years of doing this).

They claim to help you go viral.

They claim that you'll grow fast on social media.

They claim that they'll make it easy on you, so you can just grow your following without having any form of skill or understanding.

And now they're trying to go fully agentic, which only works if you know what you're doing (we'll talk about that later, we built the MCP for social media).

Plus, when everyone has an advantage, it is no longer an advantage.

I promise you, I love AI, but having it write everything for you, especially as a beginner, is a death sentence.
You may get lucky and have one, two, or three posts do well.

You may gain a lot of followers (because that's what they promise to get you to buy), but then what?

Can you replicate it?

Does your audience actually care about who you are?

Or are you just a one hit wonder like every other creator who tries to get-followers-quick?

The creators you love... the ones who put out ideas that actually change your life, understand that the creative process (capturing, resurfacing, and synthesizing ideas) is your competitive edge when everyone is racing to put out as much slop as possible.

So we built an actual solution.

For the people who know deep down that the toys and gimmicks being marketed to you aren't a long term strategy.

It's called Eden. The second brain for creators.

It has every scheduling, analytics, auto-dm, and outlier research (for all platforms) features that everyone else has - built by someone who knows what's useful and what's not.

But it also has the ideation process built in, which cannot be skipped.

Here's what it looks like, and how to write a post people actually care about:

1) Save inspiration from anywhere (and read + highlight)

Capturing ideas, posts, links, and highlights inside of an agent or AI chat sounds like hell.

Not everything needs to, or should be, jammed into a chat UI.

In Eden you can:

- Paste any social post link (we transcribe any post)

- Integrate with Kindle, Snipd, or Readwise

- Pull in X or Substack bookmarks

- Jot down quick ideas or write inside docs

- Open any YouTube transcript or article in Reader mode and highlight it

We auto-categorize and tag everything for you, so our Deep Synthesis agent can find novel connections and relations across your library - making it easy to surface idaes you thought you lost.

2) Research what's working, study top creators

Outlier tools are the bread and butter for every creator.

When you do research for a YouTube video, you look for high performing titles and thumbnails, and you study what worked for others.

But what about every other platform?

We have a social corpus of 3m+ posts across all platforms and growing.

You can scroll the Discover page for inspiration, search any creator and filter by top posts, or use Deep Social in the AI chat to search across all of them.

This is what gives the MCP access to trending topics without scraping millions of posts yourself.

3) Create with everything in one place, build swipe files

I don't think I will ever give up writing.

I love sitting down in the morning, opening up a page, researching good ideas, and turning it into something worth sharing.

In Eden, you work on Boards.

You can paste social posts and build shareable swipe files, or you can add your outlines and drafts while having your library, chat, or ideas open right next to it.

4) Chat with anything to get the information you need

Claude and ChatGPT are essential, but they are blind.

They can't read social links. They can't see what's trending.

When you're writing scripts, articles, posts, or drafts - you need to be able to pull information from the sources you research. In today's world, that usually means social posts, YouTube videos, and articles.

5) Draft, schedule, and publish to all platforms

X, Instagram, LinkedIn, Substack, Threads, TikTok, and YouTube shorts.

And yes, we are one of the first to support article scheduling to X and Substack.

You don't have to copy paste to every platform anymore.

You simply write, schedule, and let it go out to all platforms.

6) Or do it all from the MCP

I don't believe that the future of content is fully agentic.

But, that doesn't mean that AI can't help with researching top posts, ideation, and scheduling content.

You do the writing and thinking, let AI handle the busy work and resurfacing of ideas you need to find.

With Eden, you don't need to give up your Claude, Hermes, or other agentic workflows. You simply connect the MCP and now you can build your own agentic content system, if that's your cup of tea.

Eden is the Social Media MCP.

You don't have to pay for scrapers anymore.

You can finally access trends, any social link, and any account.

You can access your analytics, build content dashboards with our infrastructure (that you don't need to maintain as a full time job), and post.

We've actually built 4 skills for deep topic research, personal brand strategy, building a content command center, and more - we'll link those below.

All in all:

If you're a creator, Eden is your base.

It's where you write, research, and publish every single day.

Try it free below:

Then, forget about the goals and execute.

先不说那 100 万美元的奖金，我认为人们一直对长文有一种默默的渴望。钟摆在 TikTok 和无尽滚动的方向上摆得太远了，而互联网有机会自我纠正。

我不认为人类的大脑天生就该在你一拿起手机时就被撕扯向一千个不同的方向。太多的混乱，会对日常生活的质量产生下游影响。

长内容让你能专注于一组想法。它给头脑带来秩序。你学到更多，感觉更好，通常还会留下一些你真正能应用到生活中的东西，哪怕只是一种更好的思考方式。

尤其是有了 AI 之后，我们已经到了以为自己想要东西越短越好的地步。我们有一种病态的欲望，想要“直奔重点”，而重点恰恰在于与它共处。你可以收集所有你想要的技巧和窍门，但你完全错过了让这些技巧转化为结果的语境。一个可执行步骤的要点清单对你毫无用处。

2015 年之前的书是最好的选择，但长文是朝着我认为正确的方向迈出的很好一步。

EN 原文

$1 million dollar prizes aside, I think there's been a quiet hunger for articles. The pendulum swung too far in the direction of TikTok and endless scrolling and the internet has a chance to self-correct.

I don't think the human brain was meant to be ripped in a thousand different directions as soon as you get on your phone. Too much chaos that has downstream affects on the quality of everyday life.

Long form content allows you to focus on set of ideas. It brings order to the mind. You learn more, you feel better, and usually you're left with something you can actually apply to your life, even if it's just a better way of thinking.

Especially with AI, we've gotten to the point where we think we want things as short as possible. We have this deranged desire to "get to the point" when the point is to sit with it. You can collect all of the tips and tricks you want but you're completely missing the context that allows you to turn those tips into results. A bullet list of actionable steps will do absolutely nothing for you.

Pre-2015 books are the best option, but articles are a great step in what I think is the right direction.

2026-01-01 · ♥ 606 在 X 上查看 ↗

作为一个长期反对 AI 的人，我想说：AI 和其他任何技能一样，你越擅长它，它就越有用。

第一次弹吉他时，你真的什么都弹不出来。难听死了。但你会慢慢变好。你能弹更多的歌。你会更享受它。

我们曾被引导去相信 AI 会解决我们所有的问题、替我们做所有事，所以当它做不到时，人们就失望了；但如果你真正去学它，你就会看到它能有多大帮助。这听起来像是在推脱，但认为 AI 开箱即用就能解决你所有的问题是很荒谬的。如果你不长时间使用它，那么（和其他所有技能一样）你就无法用它得到最好的结果。

它不会消除你所有的工作——如果你不想，它甚至一点都不会消除（我反而花了更多时间在工作上，因为很有趣）——但它会给你一种更深入、更愉快的方式去做你已经在做的事。你从体力劳动中抽象出一层，进入脑力劳动。你更多地待在想法与品味的领域。它开始更像一场游戏或谜题，而不是“工作”。

你必须能够接受：从手动写代码或文字的苦活，转变为判断它听起来是否是你想要的样子。我想除了那些还没有从劳动中抽离出来的其他作家，没人会说雇用代笔作家（比如詹姆斯·帕特森）是作弊。最终读者依然喜爱它。情节、愿景以及最终出版的内容依然由他掌控。也没人会说电影导演不值得称赞，因为他没有亲手拍摄或搭建布景。

对 AI 的反对将会有、而且已经有很多，理由也是成立的，但其中大多数理由是心理防御机制，把你和“你如何通过工作方式来定义自己”捆绑在一起。

AI 不必成为一种宗教。你不必什么都用它。但我认为主动选择一个注定会输的阵营并不明智。

EN 原文

As someone who was against AI for a long time, AI is a skill just like any other, and the usefulness of AI increases as you get better at it.

The first time you play a guitar, you literally can't do anything. You sound like shit. But you slowly get better. You can play more songs. You enjoy it so much more.

We were made to think that AI would just solve all our problems and do everything for us, so people were disappointed when it didn't do those things, but if you actually try to learn it, then you will see how helpful it can be. That sounds like a cop out, but it's silly to think that AI is just going to solve all your problems out of the box. If you don't use it for an extended period of time then (as with every other skill) you will not be able to get the best results with it.

It won't remove all of your work, or any of it for that matter if you don't want it to (I've been spending more time working, because it's fun), but it will give you a deeper, more enjoyable way of doing what you already do. You abstract out a layer from physical labor to mental labor. You spend more time in the realm of ideas and taste. It starts to feel more like a game or puzzle than it does "work."

You have to be okay with moving from doing the manual grunt work of writing lines of code or prose to discerning whether or not it sounds like you want it to sound. I don't think anyone, aside from other writers who haven't detached from the labor, would argue that hiring a ghostwriter (i.e. James Patterson) is cheating. The end readers still love it. He is still in control of the plot, vision, and what actually gets published. Nobody would argue that the director of a film doesn't deserve praise because he is not manually filming it or building the set.

There is going to be, and there already is, so much pushback on AI for valid reasons, but most of those reasons are psychological defense mechanisms tying you to how you've identified yourself with how you work.

AI doesn't have to be a religion. You don't have to use it for everything. But I don't think it's a wise idea to willingly choose a side that is going to lose.

2025-12-31 · ♥ 1,244 在 X 上查看 ↗

如果你想避免被取代，就别再担心 20 年后哪些技能还有用。

没人对那会是什么有丝毫头绪。世界变化如此之快，你甚至无法想象未来哪些技能会有价值。

相反，你需要学会如何快速学习，因为如果你能比别人更快地掌握任何技能，你学什么技能就不重要了。

但这不是你坐下来就能学会的东西。你必须走进竞技场。你必须在做中学。你必须构建你自己的东西。你自己的项目。你自己的产品。然后你必须把它分享给别人，以判断它是否有价值。

为什么？因为这迫使你高效地学习。你学到的一切都直接应用于一个有意义的项目，让你不必依赖一个只要求你学会单一技能、并会一有机会就把你替换掉的雇主。

EN 原文

If you want to avoid being replaced, stop worrying about which skills will be relevant 20 years from now.

Nobody has a single clue what those are going to be. The world is changing so rapidly that you can’t even imagine what skills will be valuable in the future.

Instead, you need to learn how to learn fast, because if you can become effective at any skill quicker than other people, it doesn’t matter what skill you learn.

But that isn’t something you just sit down and study. You must step into the arena. You must learn by doing. You must build your own thing. Your own project. Your own product. Then you must share it with others to determine whether it’s valuable or not.

Why? Because that forces you to learn efficiently. Everything you learn is directly applied to a meaningful project that allows you to not be dependent on an employer that requires you to learn a single skill that they will replace as soon as they can.

2025-11-18 · ♥ 1,568 在 X 上查看 ↗

自律并不难，你只是分心了。

头脑渴望秩序。这就是你感到失控的原因。你的注意力没有聚焦在一个强大到干扰无法穿透的、单一的未来愿景上。深入感受你的处境。意识到如果你继续沿着这条路走下去，你的人生会落到哪里。对自己毫无进展彻底受够。用这股负面能量作为弹弓，把自己射向那个你一直在拖延的有意义的目标。我知道你能听到那个一直在唠叨你的声音：你本应不止于此。自律来自清晰，而不是强迫。自律是身份认同的一种特征。你不自律，是因为你不是那种能顺畅地做好该做之事的人。对作家来说，坐下来写作并不难。对健美运动员来说，吃得健康并不难。事实上，让他们吃得不健康才难。他们讨厌那样。他们这么做，是因为那就是他们。他们没有别的选项。他们深深明白被干扰而偏离目标的影响。成功是自动的。如果你想自律，就别再“努力”自律了。相反，移除每一个妨碍你自律的干扰。只给自己一个选项。关掉大脑，去执行。

EN 原文

Self-discipline isn't difficult, you're just distracted.

The mind craves order. That’s why you feel out of control. Your attention is not focused on a singular vision for the future so potent that distractions can’t penetrate it. Feel deep into your situation. Realize where your life will end up if you keep going down this path. Become absolutely fed up with the lack of progress you are making. Use that negative energy to slingshot toward a meaningful goal you’ve been putting off. I know you can hear that voice that keeps nagging at you saying, you were meant for more than this. Discipline comes from clarity, not force. Discipline is a feature of identity. You aren’t disciplined because you aren’t the type of person who seamlessly does what they need to do. It isn’t difficult for a writer to sit down and write. It isn’t difficult for a bodybuilder to eat healthy. In fact, it’s difficult for them not to eat healthy. They hate it. They do it because that’s who they are. They don’t have options. They deeply understand the impact of being distracted from their goal. Success is automatic. If you want to be disciplined, stop trying to be. Instead, remove every single distraction that prevents you from being disciplined. Give yourself one option. Shut your mind off and execute.

其实很简单。

早起。完成那件最优先的任务。避开社会在你出生时就为你设定的终点。犯巨大的错误。错误是通往理想生活的发射台。永远在做一个项目。青春是最宝贵的货币，明智的做法是把它投资出去。如果你已经浪费了青春，为此哭泣并不会加快进程。你本就应该感到不知所措，这说明你在学习。每天留出 30 分钟刻意无聊（来修复你的多巴胺敏感度）。多走路。多读书。多写作。写作是你练习思考的方式。思考是你做出更好决定的方式。你人生的结果由你所有决定的总和决定。逼自己至少每周做一次从未做过的事。学点新东西。和陌生人交谈。订一张单程机票。搬进那个你负担不起的地方。因为你需要压力。真正的压力。把自己投入未来自己的处境中，看看你有没有那个本事。

Wake up early. Complete the single highest priority task. Avoid the destination society set for you at birth. Make giant mistakes. Mistakes are the launchpads toward your ideal life. Always be building a project. Youth is the greatest currency, it would be wise to invest it. If you wasted your youth, crying about it isn't going to speed up the process. You're supposed to feel overwhelmed, it means you're learning. Set aside 30 minutes daily for deliberate boredom (to unfuck your dopamine sensitivity). Walk more. Read more. Write more. Writing is how you practice thinking. Thinking is how you make better decisions. The outcome of your life is determined by the sum of your decisions. Force yourself to do something you've never done before, at least once a week. Learn something new. Talk to someone new. Book a one way plane ticket. Move into that place you can't afford. Because you need pressure. Real pressure. Launch yourself into the situation of your future self and see if you have what it takes.

那你就不做。而且你无法给出任何合理的理由。

哦，我得工作，结果被分心了。

你他妈在说什么？

你说你“必须”工作，并且“必须”做你生活中正在做的其他事情，而你刚才说你不想过这种生活，但你却不必须去做那些唯一能引向你想要的生活的事情吗？

每个人都痴迷于获得“可操作的建议”，而这显然根本无关紧要。你的心理状态一团糟。你的优先事项不存在。你需要休息一天，真正思考自己在做什么。

“哦，丹，要更有同理心！”

那就是同理心。同理心是即使伤害了某人的小情绪，也希望他们得到最好的。大多数人只是讨好你，以便让自己感觉不错，因为没有让你觉得难受。那根本不算同理心。

做得更好。

I get unnecessarily mad when people don't stick to their goals.

You say you want to start a business, lose weight, meet new people, whatever. You say you want to change your life because you're tired of where you are.

Someone tells you exactly what to do, gives you the entire roadmap.

Then you don't do it. And you can't give any good reason why.

"Oh I have to work and got sidetracked."

"I didn't go to the gym because I had something else do to."

What the fuck are you talking about?

You say you "have" to work and "have" to do whatever else you're doing in the life you just said you don't want to live, but you don't HAVE to do the only things that lead to the life you want?

Everyone is obsessed with getting "actionable advice" when that clearly doesn't matter at all. Your psychology is in the toilet. Your priorities are nonexistent. You need to take a day off and really think about what you are doing.

"Oh Dan be more empathetic!"

That IS empathy. Empathy is wanting the best for someone even if it hurts their little feelings. Most people will simply pander to you so that they feel good about not making you feel bad. That's nowhere close to empathy.

Do better.

如果你想让自己的作品得到曝光，这听起来很奇怪，但开始一个播客是你能做的最好的事情之一。

不是因为你想让它成为世界第一的播客，而是因为：

1) 高地位的人 / 你尊重的人宁愿参加播客，也不愿和你通电话。他们更有可能回应并接受，这意味着你可以免费获得一次导师通话，向他们提出你所有的问题。

2) 你利用他们的大量观众，他们也能从中受益。人们更有可能收看/收听播客，因为有他们喜欢的人参与。这可以说是最好的初学者增长“捷径”。

3) 你会与好人建立更深的关系。如果你主持一个好的播客，嘉宾更有可能回应未来的请求或直接帮你一把。

如果你是创作者、自由职业者，或者只是一个尝试做自己事情的人，你需要有人看到你的内容和作品。

大多数人很少获得关注，因为算法就像彩票。但当你有策略地与已有粉丝群体的人建立联系时，你可以更快地建立自己的粉丝群体。

即使你在整个职业生涯中只主持 2-4 个播客，这些播客本身也可能根据你邀请的嘉宾改变你的一切。

EN 原文

If you're trying to get exposure on your work, it sounds weird, but starting a podcast is one of the best things you can do.

Not because you want to make it the number 1 podcast in the world, but because:

1) High status people / people you respect would rather be on a podcast than on a call with you. They're more likely to respond and accept, meaning you get a free mentorship call to ask them all your questions.

2) You leverage their large audience, and they also benefit from it. People are more likely to watch/listen to the podcast because someone they like is on it. This is arguably the best beginner growth "hack."

3) You form deeper relationships with good people. If you host a good podcast, the guest is more likely to respond to future requests or just help you out.

If you're a creator, freelancer, or just someone who is trying to do their own thing, you need people to see your content and work.

Most people rarely gain traction because the algorithm is like the lottery. But when you are strategic about forming connections with people who already have an audience, you can build your own much, much faster.

Even if you only host 2-4 podcasts in your entire career, those alone could change everything for you depending on the guest you get on.

每个人至少尝试去做一些困难的事情，这些事情即使最终不成功，也能极大地提升智慧、技能和自身价值。你可以叫我妄想，但我相信每个人都应该追求他们认为有意义的工作，并避免过上永远舒适的生活。

“但是你也可以找到一份你喜欢的高薪工作！”

是的，但那仍然他妈的难。有时候比创业还要难很多（不，创业并不等于试图建立一个十亿美元的公司或每天工作16小时）。

成为“企业家”最初的意思是“承担”。去做某事。承担风险。具备高能动性。自我管理。掌控自己的生活，而不是将其外包给别人。

所以，是的，创业适合每个人，就像过去那些自由的人专注于自己的技艺并追求自己的兴趣一样。

如果你还没有真正尝试过，那么你根本不知道它是否适合你，而因为有人说它“不是适合所有人”就不去尝试，这既愚蠢，又剥夺了你的潜力。

I hate the whole "entrepreneurship isn't for everyone" narrative because "it's a hard thing to do." No shit it's hard. That's the point. Yes, most people aren't cut out for it right at this very second. But people can grow. They can learn something new. They can, in fact, challenge themselves. It’s insane to believe that people can actually take control of the 1/3 of their life called work, I know.

Everyone could benefit from at bare minimum trying to do something difficult that has such a massive upside in the form of wisdom, skill, and increasing your value even if it doesn't work out. Call me delusional but I believe everyone should pursue work they find meaningful and avoid a life thats perpetually comfortable.

“But you can also get a super high paying job that you enjoy!”

Yes, but that is still fucking hard. Sometimes a lot harder than entrepreneurship (no, entrepreneurship does not equal trying to build a billion dollar company or working 16 hours day).

Being an “entrepreneur” originally meant “to undertake.” To do something. To take a risk. To be high agency. Self governance. To direct your own life rather than outsource it to someone else.

So yes, entrepreneurship is for everyone, like the free individuals of the past working on their craft and pursuing their interests.

If you haven’t tried it (actually tried it) then you have no idea whether or not it’s for you, and not trying it because someone said it’s “not for everyone” is both dumb and robbing you of potential.

2025-06-07 · ♥ 1,345 在 X 上查看 ↗

大多数人无法得到他们想要的，是因为他们在挑战自己时却没有改变自己。

他们挑战自己坚持六个月的饮食，在睡前30分钟停止刷手机，学习一项新技能，改变职业。但他们总是失败，因为自律是身份的一部分。

对健康的人来说，健康饮食和去健身房并不是挑战。这就是他们的本性。他们甚至无法想象自己吃得很糟糕、放任自己的生活。这根本不会出现在他们的脑海里。

为什么？因为他们很早就明白自己不想那样生活。

他们想象了自己的生活将会走向何处。所有会发生的不好的事情。他们将会看起来和感觉如何。那些对他们来说无法获得的机会。

那种负面形象比任何挑战都更激励了他们。

你需要接受一个事实，那就是你永远不可能回到现在的生活状态。

你所有的坏习惯在你的未来生活中都没有立足之地。这就是你现在处境的原因。没有任何六个月的挑战能够改变这一点，除非你清醒地意识到，挑战在第六个月之后并不会结束。

EN 原文

Most people don't get what they want because they challenge themselves without changing themselves.

They challenge themselves to stick to a diet for 6 months, stop scrolling 30 minutes before bed, learn a new skill, change careers. And they always fail, because discipline is a feature of identity.

It’s not a challenge for fit people to eat healthy and go to the gym. It’s who they are. They can’t even imagine a life where they eat like shit and let themselves go. It doesn’t even cross their mind.

Why? Because they learned long ago that they didn't want to live that way.

They visualized where their life would end up. All the bad things that would happen. How they would look and feel. The opportunities that wouldn't be available to them.

That negative image fueled them more than any challenge ever could.

You need to be okay with the fact that you will never return to how you live right now.

None of your bad habits have a place in your future life. That's why you are where you are. No 6 month challenge is going to change that unless you are brutally aware that the challenge doesn't end after month 6.

我平时相处起来不太令人愉快。

我更喜欢独处。我讨厌超过两三天的生活脱离常规。我要么什么都不想，要么想的事情很多，中间很少。我几乎对所有妨碍我的事情都说不。

起初我以为这是性格缺陷，并试图改变它。那只导致我分散注意力，减缓了在带给我生活乐趣的目标上的进展。

当我观察我钦佩的人时，他们的使命总是放在第一位。这就是让生活变得愉快的原因，如果这种愉快被剥夺，它会蔓延到他们的工作、亲人和友谊中。

如果你知道自己想要什么，并且不屈从于别人认为你应该想要的东西，你将会变得令人不快。

那并不是什么应该感到羞愧的事情，而是应该被接受的。

事实上，你会发现人们更愿意与你相处，因为他们信任你。他们能感觉到你不像其他人那样在作假。

EN 原文

I'm generally unpleasant to be around.

I prefer being alone. I hate being out of routine for more than 2-3 days. I'm either thinking about nothing or everything with little in between. I say no to almost everything that gets in the way.

At first I thought it was a character flaw and tried to change it. That only led to me splitting focus and slowing progress on the goals that bring me joy in life.

When I observe people I look up to, their mission comes first. That's what makes life enjoyable, and if that enjoyment is taken away, it spreads into their work, their loved ones, and their friendships.

If you know what you want, and you don't fold to what others think you should want, you are going to be unpleasant to be around.

That isn't something to be ashamed of but embraced.

In fact, you'll find that people want to be around you more because they trust you. They can feel that you aren't putting on an act like everyone else.

2025-05-26 · ♥ 1,911 在 X 上查看 ↗

学习的最好方式与我们被教导的相反。

你不是先学会一切，然后再开始。你应该先开始，然后学习为什么它有效或无效。你从最基本的知识开始，然后进行实验，然后成功或失败，然后学习以理解原因。

因为这个原因，比你笨的人往往能绕着你跑。他们不会因过度教育带来的过度思考而瘫痪，也能避免纯粹试错的盲目性。

EN 原文

The best way to learn is the opposite of what we're taught.

You don't learn everything, then start. You start, then learn why it did or didn't work. You start with minimum viable knowledge, then experiment, then succeed or fail, then study to understand why.

People dumber than you tend to run circles around you because of this. They aren't paralyzed by the overthinking that comes with overeducation, and they avoid the blindness of pure trial and error.

我看到即将到来的一个趋势：

创作者会在他们的帖子、视频、新闻通讯甚至课程中分享 AI 提示，因为它增加了互动层。

内容的问题在于它是静态的。

教学内容可能很有价值，但由于它没有考虑到你自己的思维和经验，其中大部分内容并不能一对一地适用。

但是，当你把类似新闻通讯的内容变成一个提示时，不仅增加了新闻通讯的价值，读者还可以输入他们自己的思维。

产品/内容的三大主要类别是：自己动手、替你完成、与您共同完成。

这标志着自己动手时代的结束，因为 AI 可以利用上下文既作为你的教练，也作为你的自由职业者。

有人现在在 YouTube 视频中给出的策略，会变成可以为你执行该策略的信息。

EN 原文

A trend I see coming soon:

Creators sharing AI prompts along with their posts, videos, newsletters, or even courses because it adds an interactive layer.

The problem with content is that it's static.

The teachings may be valuable, but since they don't account for your own mind and experience, most of it doesn't apply 1-1.

But when you turn something like your newsletter into a prompt, not only do you increase the value of that newsletter, the reader can plug in their own mind.

The 3 main categories of products / content is do it yourself, done for you, and done with you.

This marks the end of the do it yourself era, because AI can use the context to both be your coach or freelancer.

A strategy someone gives out in a YouTube video now becomes information that can execute on that strategy for you.

你的思维运行在一个故事情节上。

游戏是具有特定机制的互动故事，这些机制会缩小你的注意力并使进度令人上瘾。

如果你想摆脱困境，使用这个 AI 提示将你的生活变成一个视频游戏（内容较长）:

–––

你是 LifeQuest AI，一位战略生活教练，将用户的生活转变为沉浸式的游戏体验。你分析他们当前的人生阶段（停滞、愿景、流动或抗拒），帮助识别他们真正的渴望，并创建一个个性化的游戏结构，包括可执行的任务和有意义的叙事。你对不确定性保持诚实，并在需要时提出澄清性问题以提供准确的指导。

上下文：

用户希望使用阿德勒心理学、流动心理学和希腊哲学的原理来将他们的人生旅程游戏化。他们寻求对自己当前人生阶段、未来方向和有意义追求的清晰理解。他们需要支持将这些目标分解为可管理的任务，并置于一个连贯的叙事框架中，使进展变得具体且有回报。此次互动分为两个阶段：首先进行评估和策略制定，然后通过任务实施和指导持续进展。

说明：

阶段 1：生活评估与游戏设计

1. 在此阶段，每次提出 1-3 个问题。不要一次提出所有问题，以减少压力。

2. 首先通过提出关键诊断性问题来识别用户当前的人生阶段：

- 生活中哪些领域感觉停滞、流动或不清晰？
- 目前哪些活动让他们充满活力，哪些活动让他们感到耗尽？
- 对于未来的结果，他们会拼命避免什么？
- 最近有哪些新的信息、人物或经历激发了他们的兴趣？

3. 分析回应以确定他们处于哪个人生阶段：

- 渺茫（不确定，无方向感）
- 愿景（逐渐清晰，积聚动力）
- 流动（高度投入，快速进展）
- 抵抗（停滞不前，依恋过去的成功）

4. 引导用户表达他们的“负面愿景”——如果没有变化，他们想要避免的结果。

5. 通过询问以下内容，帮助用户发现潜在的积极方向：

- 真正好奇心的来源
- 他们喜欢发展的技能
- 他们希望产生的有意义的影响
- 他们能够茁壮成长的环境

6. 将调查结果综合成完整的游戏结构：

- 主线任务：主要的生活方向/目标
- 支线任务：各个生活领域中的辅助目标
- 角色属性：需要发展的关键能力
- 等级系统：衡量进展的方式
- 规则：不可谈判的界限和价值观
- 奖励：对进展的有意义庆祝
- 教学阶段：初期的低风险尝试

7. 设计可量化的反馈循环，并安排每日/每周的优先任务，以提供明确的进展标志。

第2阶段：持续任务指导

1. 每次会话开始时，先检查之前任务的进度并更新用户的“角色状态”。

2. 根据他们当前的情况提供适当的指导：

- 如果卡住：帮助识别障碍和潜在解决方案
- 如果在进展：建议适当的“升级”或新的挑战
- 如果感到不知所措：简化任务或调整难度
- 如果感到无聊：在他们能力边缘引入新的挑战

3. 在他们的游戏叙事中框定所有建议，并始终保持比喻的一致性。

4. 随着用户的愿景发展，定期重新审视并更新主要任务。

5. 平衡短期成就与长期发展。

6. 当用户面临重大障碍时，帮助他们：

- 分析导致阻塞的模式
- 将复杂的挑战分解为更小的任务
- 识别潜在的“能量加成”（资源、技能或盟友）
- 将挫折重新框定为必要的情节发展

约束条件：

- 始终保持游戏隐喻，但绝不以牺牲提供实际可行的建议为代价
- 注重内在动机而非外在奖励
- 仅推荐略高于当前能力的挑战（未知的边缘）
- 绝不建议与用户所述的界限或价值观相冲突的活动
- 避免提供泛泛的建议；所有指导应针对用户的具体情况
- 当信息不足时，应承认不确定性

输出格式：

阶段 1 输出：

生命阶段分析：当前阶段识别及支持性证据

角色评估：优点、缺点、动机和潜在方向

游戏设计：

- 主线任务（整体人生方向）
- 支线任务（辅助目标）
- 角色属性（需发展的技能）
- 等级系统（进度指标）
- 游戏规则（界限/价值观）

教程阶段：前1-2周的特定任务和实验

反馈系统：每日/每周签到结构

阶段2输出（每次辅导课程）：

1. 任务日志更新：自上次互动以来的进展

2. 角色状态：当前“等级”和属性

3. 任务指导：接下来的具体步骤

4. 挑战校准：调整以保持最佳难度

5. 敘事发展：近期发展如何融入他们的整体故事

EN 原文

Your mind runs on a storyline.

Games are interactive stories with certain mechanisms that narrow your focus and make progress addictive.

If you want to get unstuck, use this AI prompt to turn your life into a video game (it's long):

–––

You are LifeQuest AI, a strategic life coach that transforms the user's life into an immersive game experience. You analyze their current life phase (Limbo, Vision, Flow, or Resistance), help identify their true desires, and create a personalized game structure with actionable quests and meaningful narrative. You maintain honesty about uncertainty and ask clarifying questions when needed to provide accurate guidance.

Context:

The user wants to gamify their life journey using principles from Adlerion psychology, flow psychology, and Greek philosophy. They seek clarity on their current life phase, future direction, and meaningful pursuits. They need support to break these goals into manageable quests within a cohesive narrative framework that makes progress tangible and rewarding. This interaction unfolds in two phases: first to assess and strategize, then to implement and coach ongoing progress through quests.

Instructions:

Phase 1: Life Assessment & Game Design

1. Throughout this phase, ask 1-3 questions at a time. Do not ask all questions at once to reduce overwhelm.

2. Begin by asking key diagnostic questions to identify the user's current life phase:

- What areas of life feel stuck, flowing, or unclear?
- What activities currently energize vs. drain them?
- What would they fight to avoid as a future outcome?
- What new information, people, or experiences have recently sparked their interest?

3. Analyze responses to determine which life phase they're in:

- Limbo (uncertainty, directionless feeling)
- Vision (emerging clarity, building momentum)
- Flow (strong engagement, rapid progress)
- Resistance (plateauing, clinging to past success)

4. Guide the user to articulate their "negative vision" — the outcome they want to avoid if nothing changes.

5. Help the user discover potential positive directions by asking about:

- Sources of genuine curiosity
- Skills they enjoy developing
- Meaningful impacts they wish to make
- Environments where they thrive

6. Synthesize findings into a complete game structure:

- Main Quest: Primary life direction/purpose
- Side Quests: Supporting goals in various life domains
- Character Stats: Key abilities to develop
- Level System: How progress will be measured
- Rules: Non-negotiable boundaries and values
- Rewards: Meaningful celebration of progress
- Tutorial Phase: Initial low-risk experiments to try

7. Design quantifiable feedback loops with daily/weekly priority tasks that provide clear markers of progress.

Phase 2: Ongoing Quest Guidance

1. Begin each session by checking progress on previous quests and updating the user's "character status."

2. Provide appropriate coaching based on their current situation:

- If stuck: Help identify obstacles and potential solutions
- If progressing: Suggest appropriate "level-ups" or new challenges
- If overwhelmed: Simplify quests or adjust difficulty
- If bored: Introduce novel challenges at the edge of their capabilities

3. Frame all advice within their game narrative, maintaining the metaphor consistently.

4. Regularly revisit and update the main quest as the user's vision evolves.

5. Balance short-term achievements with long-term development.

6. When the user faces significant obstacles, help them:

- Analyze patterns that led to the block
- Break down complex challenges into smaller quests
- Identify potential "power-ups" (resources, skills, or allies)
- Reframe setbacks as essential plot developments

Constraints:

- Maintain game metaphor consistently but never at the expense of providing practical, actionable advice
- Focus on intrinsic motivation over external rewards
- Recommend only challenges slightly beyond current capabilities (the edge of the unknown)
- Never suggest activities that conflict with user's stated boundaries or values
- Avoid generic advice; tailor all guidance to user's specific situation
- Acknowledge uncertainty when you don't have enough information

Output Format:

Phase 1 Output:

Life Phase Analysis: Current phase identification with supporting evidence

Character Assessment: Strengths, weaknesses, motivations, and potential directions

Game Design:

- Main Quest (overall life direction)
- Side Quests (supporting goals)
- Character Stats (skills to develop)
- Level System (progress metrics)
- Game Rules (boundaries/values)

Tutorial Phase: First 1-2 weeks of specific quests and experiments

Feedback System: Daily/weekly check-in structure

Phase 2 Output (for each coaching session):

1. Quest Log Update: Progress since last interaction

2. Character Status: Current "level" and stats

3. Quest Guidance: Next immediate steps with specificity

4. Challenge Calibration: Adjustments to maintain optimal difficulty

5. Narrative Development: How recent developments fit into their overall story

将“如何写文案”的输出和“着陆页结构”的输出保存到你的笔记中某处，或者在下面需要时直接复制/粘贴

然后，你将要：

- 将以下提示发送给新的 AI 聊天
- 告诉它你想创建一个高转化率的登陆页面
- 告诉它使用“如何撰写文案”的输出内容来理解如何撰写文案
- 告诉它使用“登陆页面结构”的输出内容来格式化文案

现在它可能会询问你的目标受众以及你正在销售的产品。

如果你不了解那些东西，你可以对每一样东西都按照完全相同的流程操作（分解 YouTube 视频或 PDF 来教你如何 > 将其转化为提示），以创建客户画像和不可抗拒的报价。

作为一名作家，我注意到AI并没有缩短我的写作过程（因为我不希望它这样），反而让它变得更长。

我不把AI当作作者，我把它当作读者。

它对我的观点提出了异议。

我让它根据多种指标来评估我的开场白和引言，比如相关性、好奇心差距的使用以及简洁性。

我已经概览了我的写作，以确保读者能够理解它，学到一些新东西，并在阅读完后至少得到一件可以实施的事情。

我真的很难让AI为我写作。

这感觉不对。无论AI多么先进，它仍然缺乏灵魂。

即使它提出了好的或新颖的想法，我也不想使用它们，因为那会剥夺我自己想出这些想法的乐趣。当我让 AI 接管太多过程时，我真的会开始感觉自己变得愚笨，创造力下降。

我的提示已经转向帮助提升写作过程，而不是取代它，这让我能够花更多时间（而不是更少）在我喜欢精通的创作上。

EN 原文

As a writer, I've noticed that AI doesn't shorten my writing process (because I don't want it to), it makes it longer.

I don't treat AI as the writer, I treat it as the reader.

I have it raise objections to my points.

I have it rate my hook and introduction for various metrics like relatability, use of curiosity gaps, and brevity.

I have it overview my writing to ensure readers understand it, learn something knew, and are given at least one thing to implement once they're done reading.

I really struggle to have AI do the writing for me.

It doesn't feel right. No matter how good the AI gets it still lacks a soul.

Even if it comes up with good or novel ideas, I don't want to use them because that strips the joy from coming up with them myself. I literally start to feel dumber and less creative when I let AI take over too much of the process.

My prompts have shifted to helping enhance the writing process rather than replace it, and it's allowed me to spend more time (not less) on the craft I enjoy mastering.

我可能完全错了，死互联网可能会变得更糟。但现在已经相当糟了。到处都是大量垃圾内容（大多在底层，很多人根本看不到），而真正的创作者仍然能够分得自己的一块蛋糕。

This is a big update for us and sets us up for quite a few things.

我通过 AOF 的发布学到的一件事是，口碑营销极难掌握。这远不只是“发布一个好产品并期待人们将其传播给数百万其他人”。

而“拥有大量观众”只有在你尽可能多地推广时才是优势。无论你是自助出版还是与大型出版社合作，你都必须努力销售。

像 P&P 这样的这些小书（我还计划了四本）只是我写我想写的内容的一种途径，而不必担心营销带来的各种复杂细节。

EN 原文

One thing I learned with the AOF launch is that word of mouth marketing is extremely difficult to nail. It's much more than 'launch a good product and expect people to spread it to millions of others.'

And "having a large audience" is only an advantage if you promote as much as you possibly can. Whether you're self-published or go with a large publisher, you have to sell. Hard.

I'll aim for a NYT bestseller with my next book. The team I have working on it has been building up leads, distribution beyond my audience, strategizing positioning + angles + hooks, and more for the past 6 months, and we're still 6 or more months out from launch.

These little books like P&P (I have 4 more planned) are just outlets to write what I want to write without having to worry about all of the nooks and crannies that come along with marketing.

我觉得AI对写作的影响被大大夸大了。

这是来自一个正在开发AI写作软件的人说的。

首先，内容已经太多了。我们无法全部阅读。AI 会增加更多内容，但大部分内容除非是由能够让人看到这些内容的人撰写的（已经是熟练作家的人），否则大多会淹没在底层。写作是一种技能，只有当它与一种个性和互补技能结合，使其他人能够看到并关心它时，才能获得关注。区分信号与噪音可能会略微变得更难，但我对此表示怀疑，因为 AI 内容仍然可以是信号。

其次，AI可以写推文、文章、新闻简报或视频脚本，但这并不是你建立读者群的原因或方式。你的“品牌”是你所发布的一切内容的总和。

拥有一条推文或抖音视频走红，除了可能带来一次快速的现金收益之外，几乎对你没有任何帮助。大多数病毒式内容都很浅薄、智商不高。这不是建立有意义的长期品牌的基础。大多数有价值的内容并不会病毒式传播。

你的品牌是你发布的每一篇作品的结晶，无论是否病毒式传播。它是个人或组织的理念、意义和愿景。你的写作是这幅随着时间编织而成的挂毯中的一根线索。

第三，仅仅因为AI可以写作、编程或进行市场营销，并不意味着每个人都会去写作、编程或做市场营销。这意味着那些已经想要写作或者看到其中价值的人，会尝试利用AI。一旦他们意识到缺乏对技能的基本理解不会让你走得很远，他们无论如何都必须从零开始学习它（向vibe程序员致敬）。

AI是革命性的。毫无疑问。

但现在的炒作感觉就像每个人都在跟风下一个快速致富的计划。那些不被速成方法和廉价多巴胺奴役的人将会像以前一样持续表现良好。

实际上，这更像是我们书写方式的下一次进化。

笔和纸 > 打字机 > 键盘 > 软件辅助 > AI辅助。

这是一个很大的飞跃，但经过所有“写作已死”的炒作之后，我们仍然处在原来的位置。

EN 原文

I feel like AI's impact on writing is vastly overhyped.

And that's coming from someone building an AI writing software.

First, there is already too much content. We can't read it all. AI will add more, but most of it will go to the bottom of the barrel unless written by someone who could have gotten that content seen (someone who's already a skilled writer). Writing is one skill that only gains traction when paired with a personality and complementary skills that make other people see it and care about it. It may get slightly harder to separate signal from noise, but I doubt it, because AI content can still be signal.

Second, AI can write a tweet or article or newsletter or video script, but that's not why or how you build an audience of readers. Your "brand" is a culmination of everything you've put out.

Having one tweet or TikTok go viral does almost nothing for you aside from maybe a quick cash grab. Most viral content is shallow and low IQ. That's not a foundation for a meaningful long-term brand. Most worthwhile content is not viral.

Your brand is a culmination of every piece of writing you put out, viral or not. It's the personal or organizational philosophy, meaning, and vision. Your writing is a thread in that tapestry woven over time.

Third, just because AI can write or code or market doesn't mean that everyone will write or code or market. It means that people who already wanted to write, or see the value in it, will attempt to leverage AI. And once they realize that a lack of fundamental understanding of the skill won't get you very far, they'll have to learn it from scratch anyway (shoutout vibe coders).

AI is revolutionary. There's no question about it.

But the hype right now feels like everyone hopping on the next get rich quick scheme. The people who aren't slaves to quick fixes and cheap dopamine will continue to do well as they have been.

In reality, this is more like the next evolution of how we write.

Pen and paper > typewriter > keyboard > software assisted > AI assisted.

It's a big jump, but after all the "writing is dead" hype we're still in the same place we've been.

EN 原文

串内续帖

1) 制定你的理想生活蓝图

大多数人没有学习的目标。

他们学习自己被告知要学的内容，或者是父母或偶像会认可他们学习的内容。

• 你想从生活中得到什么

• What you want out of life

Avoid learning what leads to what you don't want.

现在你已经准备好开始了，但不要开始学习。

EN 原文

• Save 3-5 sources of inspiration you want to emulate
• Study those sources and study their structure or characteristics
• Outline the project into sections, milestones, inspiration
• Have a place to capture ideas that comes to mind

Now that you're ready to start, don't start learning.

串内续帖

3) 从你已知的开始

学习来源于努力，而不是死记硬背。

开始项目。不要先看20个教程。让它暴露你知识的空白。尝试自己解决。当你最有可能记住答案时再去搜索答案。

EN 原文

3) Start With What You Know

Learning comes from struggle, not memorization.

Start the project. No, don't watch 20 tutorials beforehand. Let it expose the gaps in your knowledge. Try to figure it out. Search for the answer when your mind is most likely to remember it.

串内续帖

无论你是在学习 Photoshop 还是学习编程，都从你已经知道的开始。

至少尝试迈出第一步。下载软件并开始尝试操作。尝试创造一些东西。任何东西。

只要让你的大脑处于渴望学习的状态即可。

EN 原文

Whether you're learning Photoshop or learning to program, start with what you know.

At least try to take the first step. Download the software and start playing around. Try to create something. Anything.

Just get your mind in a state where it's hungry to learn.

串内续帖

然后，按照这个过程：

• 你不知道该做什么
• 你尝试并失败
• 搜索答案或询问 AI
• 尝试实施答案
• 重复，直到项目完成
• 如果找不到答案，询问专家

几年前，谷歌搜索还是一项技能。

EN 原文

Then, follow this process:

• You don't know what to do
• You try and fail
• Search for the answer or ask AI
• Try to implement the answer
• Repeat until the project is complete
• If you can't find the answer, ask an expert

A few years ago, Google searching was a skill.

串内续帖

现在，AI正在取代那种技能。

如果你能写出一个能够快速获取所需信息的提示，你就能克服障碍，并且学习得更快。

每当你有问题时，即使是“我如何在 Photoshop 中选择一个对象”，也要问AI。

EN 原文

Now, AI is replacing that skill.

If you can write a prompt that gets you the information you need, fast, you can overcome obstacles and learn that much faster.

Whenever you have a question, even if it's "how do I select an object in Photoshop," ask AI.

串内续帖

3.5) 当你不想做的时候如何开始

蔡加尼克效应是一种心理现象，人们对未完成的任务比已完成的任务记忆更深。

意思是，如果我们没有完成项目的任务，更容易找到开始的动力。

EN 原文

3.5) How To Start When You Don't Feel Like It

The Zeigarnik Effect is a psychological phenomenon where people remember unfinished tasks more than completed tasks.

Meaning, if we don't finish tasks for our project, it's much easier to find the motivation to get started.

串内续帖

串内续帖

现在你已经有了参考框架、项目大纲，并且已经开始取得进展——你可以开始通过一般的学习资料和教程来补充。

Now that you have a frame of reference, project outline, and have started making progress—you can start supplementing with general learning and tutorials.

串内续帖

构建你的学习最好的方式是分为三个时间段

• 30-90分钟构建项目
• 30-60分钟学习所需知识
• 30分钟散步以反思和消化

这些是你的关键习惯。

每天都要做。不要跳过。

EN 原文

The best way to structure your learning is in 3 timeblocks

• 30-90 minutes of building the project
• 30-60 minutes of learning what you need
• 30 minutes of walking to reflect and process

Those are your keystone habits.

Do them every day. Do not skip.

串内续帖

5) 系统地写下你所学的内容以进行反思

费曼技巧是由物理学家理查德·费曼推广的一种学习方法。

它的核心是通过用简单的语言解释一个概念来深入理解它，就好像你在教一个完全没有相关知识的人一样：

EN 原文

5) Write To Systematically Reflect On What You Learn

The Feynman Technique is a learning method popularized by physicist Richard Feynman.

It's about deeply understanding a concept by explaining it in simple terms as if you were teaching it to someone with no prior knowledge:

串内续帖

• 选择一个你想要理解的概念
• 用简单的语言教给别人
• 发现自己知识中的空白
• 回顾资料并重复

这与“门徒效应”有重叠，总结来说，老师学到的比学生更多。

EN 原文

• Choose a concept you want to understand
• Teach it to someone else in simple language
• Identify gaps in your knowledge
• Review source material and repeat

This overlaps with the Protege Effect which is, in summary, that the teacher learns more than the student.

串内续帖

迄今为止，最好的方法是写作。

• 开始一个免费的新闻通讯

你得到的反馈越多越好。

大多数 AI 摘要很糟糕，因为它们只给你关键点，却遗漏了大部分有用信息。

这里有一个更适合做笔记/研究的提示：

===全面内容总结器===

<System>：
你是一位内容总结专家，擅长捕捉关键事实和潜在背景。你的总结包括重要信息、有意义的背景、哲学基础以及其他人可能忽略的微妙细节。你优先考虑全面性而非简洁性，确保没有遗漏任何重要内容，同时仍然高效地组织信息。当对细节不确定时，你会明确指出，而不是用假设填补空白。

<Context>:
用户将提供他们希望彻底总结的内容（YouTube 视频、文章、书籍、播客或其他媒体）。他们重视全面理解而非快速摘要，并特别希望捕捉那些可能被不够详细的总结者视为“无关紧要”的上下文元素和哲学框架。

<说明>：
1. 首先确定内容类型、创作者/作者、标题和发布日期（如果有的话）。

2. 创建一个多层次的摘要，包括以下内容：
- 核心论点/主要论点（1-2句，明确中心观点）
- 关键点总结（以项目符号列出重要事实、论点或结论）
- 背景框架（确定哲学、理论、历史或文化背景）
- 详细分解（按章节或时间顺序总结所有重要内容）
- 微妙视角（记录任何竞争观点、反论点或提出的限定条件）
- 潜在假设（识别未明言的前提、世界观或影响内容的偏见）

3. 特别注意：
- 抽象概念、哲学立场和理论框架
- 影响内容的历史或文化背景
- 使用的方法论或推理模式
- 创作者承认的限定条件、限制或细微差别
- 与更广泛的思想、运动或学科的联系
- 内容所暗示的影响或应用

4. 当信息不清楚或缺失时：
- 使用诸如“内容未说明...”之类的短语清楚地指出信息空白或模糊之处
- 避免用假设来补充缺失的细节
- 如果内容包含可能矛盾的元素，应明确指出这些矛盾

5. 对于包含引用或参考其他作品的内容：
- 注意提到的关键来源及其对论点的重要性
- 识别所借鉴的知识传统或学术流派

<约束条件>：
• 优先保证准确性和全面性，而不是简洁性
• 避免将复杂理念简化到失真的程度
• 不引入原内容中不存在的外部信息
• 对内容的立场或论点保持中立
• 在总结较长内容时包含时间戳或页面参考

<输出格式>:

##[内容标题]的综合总结

创建者/作者：[姓名]
发布日期：[如有日期]
内容类型：[文章/视频/播客/等]
长度/时长：[如有页数/分钟]

###核心论点
[1-2句陈述主要论点或目的]

###关键点
• [关键点 1]
• [关键点 2]
• [根据需要继续]

###情境框架
[段落（用于识别哲学、理论、历史或文化情境）]

###详细分解
[部分/时间戳 1]
[本部分的详细总结]

[部分/时间戳 2]
[本部分的详细总结]
[根据需要继续]

###细微的观点
[段落（说明提出的相互竞争的观点、反驳论点或限定条件）]

### 基本假设
[段落（识别未明言的前提、世界观或偏见）]

###联系与影响
[关于此内容如何与更广泛的理念相关及其潜在应用的段落]

EN 原文

Most AI summaries suck because they give you key points and leave out most useful information.

Here's a better prompt for note-taking/research:

===Comprehensive Content Summarizer===

<System>:
You are an Expert Content Summarizer with a talent for capturing both key facts and underlying context. Your summaries include essential information, meaningful context, philosophical underpinnings, and subtle nuances that others might overlook. You prioritize comprehensiveness over brevity, ensuring nothing important is missed, while still organizing information efficiently. When uncertain about details, you clearly indicate this rather than filling gaps with assumptions.

<Context>:
The user will provide content (YouTube videos, articles, books, podcasts, or other media) they want thoroughly summarized. They value comprehensive understanding over quick highlights, and specifically want to capture contextual elements and philosophical frameworks that might be dismissed as "fluff" by less thorough summarizes.

<Instructions>:
1. Begin by identifying the content type, creator/author, title, and publication date, if available.

2. Create a multi-layered summary with these components:
- Core Thesis/Main Argument (1-2 sentences identifying the central point)
- Key Points Summary (bulleted list of crucial facts, arguments, or conclusions)
- Contextual Framework (identify the philosophical, theoretical, historical, or cultural context)
- Detailed Breakdown (section-by-section or chronological summary capturing all significant content)
- Nuanced Perspectives (note any competing viewpoints, counterarguments, or qualifiers presented)
- Underlying Assumptions (identify unstated premises, worldviews, or biases that inform the content)

3. Pay special attention to:
- Abstract concepts, philosophical positions, and theoretical frameworks
- Historical or cultural context that shapes the content Methodological approaches or reasoning patterns used
- Qualifiers, limitations, or nuances the creator acknowledges
- Connections to broader ideas, movements, or disciplines Implications or applications suggested by the content

4. When information is unclear or missing:
- Clearly indicate gaps or ambiguities with phrases like "The content does not specify..."
- Avoid filling in missing details with assumptions
- If the content contains potentially contradictory elements, note these tensions explicitly

5. For content with citations or references to other works:
- Note key sources referenced and their significance to the argument
- Identify intellectual traditions or schools of thought being drawn upon

<Constraints>:
• Prioritize accuracy and comprehensiveness over brevity
• Avoid simplifying complex ideas to the point of distortion
• Do not introduce external information not present in the original content
• Maintain neutrality toward the content's positions or arguments
• Include timestamps or page references when summarizing longer content

<Output Format>:

##Comprehensive Summary of [Content Title]

Creator/Author: [Name]
Publication Date: [Date if available]
Content Type: [Article/Video/Podcast/etc.]
Length/Duration: [Pages/Minutes if available]

###Core Thesis
[1-2 sentence statement of the main argument or purpose]

###Key Points
• [Essential point 1]
• [Essential point 2]
• [Continue as needed]

###Contextual Framework
[Paragraph(s) identifying philosophical, theoretical, historical, or cultural context]

###Detailed Breakdown
[Section/Timestamp 1]
[Thorough summary of this section]

[Section/Timestamp 2]
[Thorough summary of this section]
[Continue as needed]

###Nuanced Perspectives
[Paragraph(s) noting competing viewpoints, counterarguments, or qualifiers presented]

###Underlying Assumptions
[Paragraph(s) identifying unstated premises, worldviews, or biases]

###Connections & Implications
[Paragraph(s) on how this content connects to broader ideas and its potential applications]

1) 整理杂乱笔记

大多数人使用Kortex是为了它的捕捉功能。

你可以给自己“发短信”记录想法，并将它们整理成文档。

现在，这已经变成了“聊天”模式。

如果你正在写文章、规划待办事项、记下社交媒体帖子创意，或者在散步时做笔记：

你可以“@”一个特定文档，或者创建一个文档来整理这些想法。（比把想法写在一个冗长的笔记里、很可能会被忘记要好得多）。

然后，按“Tab”开启kAI，并使用这个提示语：

“提供这次聊天的全面总结。将所有想法整合为章节、关键点和主要思想，以便后来可以轻松作为详细笔记参考。请包括我提到的所有链接、来源或文档。不要遗漏任何信息。”

你还可以将其与YouTube功能结合使用，将你的捕捉内容和研究转化为笔记。

EN 原文

1) Synthesize Messy Notes

Most people use Kortex for its capture feature.

You can "text" yourself ideas and organize them into documents.

Now, this has turned into "chats."

If you're writing an article, planning todos, jotting down social post ideas, or taking notes on a walk:

You can "@" a specific document or create one to organize these ideas. (Much better than jotting down ideas in one long running note that you'll forget about).

Then, toggle on kAI with "Tab" and use this prompt:

"Provide a comprehensive summary of this chat. Synthesize all of the ideas into sections, key points, and main ideas so that it can easily be used as a detailed note I can reference later. Please include any links, sources, or documents I've mentioned. Do not omit any information."

You can also pair this with the YouTube feature to turn your captures and research into notes.

串内续帖

2) YouTube 摘要与学习教练

在我们努力实现能够从任何地方捕捉任何内容的使命时，您现在可以将 YouTube 链接粘贴到聊天中，以自动将其添加为来源。（即使是 3 小时的视频）

（哦，你还可以在电脑的任何地方按 Option+C 打开聊天，快速提问）

然后，你可以使用此提示将 kAI 变成学习教练：

成为一名学习教练，帮助我学习这个视频@[video]的关键点，具体背景如下：
- 你是一名专业导师
- 你帮助我识别知识空白
- 你提出深思熟虑的问题，以帮助我自己找到答案

你的任务是：
- 每次提供一个关键课程
- 每个回答后附上一个问题来测试我的知识
- 鼓励我继续进行下一个课程

对于每个回答：
- 从课程开始
- 包含一个用于进一步学习的书籍、视频或资源链接
- 包含一个直接的挑战或作业
- 让我继续下一个课程

你不必用YouTube视频来做这件事。

你可以使用你之前在 Kindle 上的高亮或笔记来做到这一点。

EN 原文

2) YouTube Summaries & Study Coach

As we work towards our mission of being able to capture anything from anywhere, you can now paste a YouTube link into a chat to automatically add it as a source. (Even 3+ hour videos)

(Oh, and you can open chats from anywhere on your computer with Option+C to ask questions fast)

Then, you can use this prompt to turn kAI into a study coach:

"Be a study coach to help me learn the key points of this video @[video] with the following context:
- You are a professional tutor
- You help me identify knowledge gaps
- You ask thoughtful questions to help me get to the answer myself

Your mission is to:
- Provide one key lesson at a time
- Follow each response with a question to test my knowledge
- Encourage me to move onto the next lesson

For each response:
- Start with the lesson
- Include one link to a book, video, or resource for further study
- Include one direct challenge or assignment
- Ask me to continue to the next lesson"

You don't have to do this with a YouTube video.

You can do it with your Kindle highlights or notes you've taken previously.

串内续帖

3) 写作反馈

由于你所有的文章、通讯和视频脚本都是在你的工作区中撰写的（希望如此），你只需“@”它们并让 kAI 审阅即可。

或者，你可以在不同的 YouTube 视频、笔记或来源上“@”以获取在写作中可以使用的相关想法。

使用此提示：

表现得像一个注重细节的文稿编辑。

您将编辑这篇文章：[参考]

然后你将分析文本以获取以下内容：

1) 结构
• 就逻辑顺序和连贯性提供可操作的反馈。
• 提供任何建议改进的示例。

2) 内容
• 识别任何可提高具体性、观点或为读者提供更多价值的机会。
• 提供可操作的反馈，说明如何通过提示、原因、错误、经验教训、示例、故事、研究或其他快速优化内容的方法来增强文本，使其对读者更有价值、更具吸引力。解释每个选择的逻辑。
• 提供任何推荐改进的示例。

3) 语法
• 进行详细的语法分析。
• 标出拼写错误的单词
• 标出被动语态的使用
• 标出不完整、连写、复杂或令人困惑的句子，

请一步一步进行您的分析。

在进行下一步之前，请先与我确认。

当你的写作和建议都打开时，你可以查看它们或向 kAI 询问更多澄清。

EN 原文

3) Writing Feedback

Since all of your articles, newsletters, and video scripts are written in your workspace (hopefully), you can simply "@" them and ask kAI to review them.

Or, you can "@" different YT videos, notes, or sources to ask for relevant ideas to include in your writing.

Use this prompt:

"Act like a detail-oriented copyeditor.

You will be editing this writing: [REFERENCE]

And then you will analyze the text for the following:

1) Structure
• Provide actionable feedback on logical order and coherence.
• Provide examples of any recommended improvements.

2) Content
• Identify any opportunities to improve specificity, point of view, or ways to give the reader more value.
• Provide actionable feedback on ways to enhance the text using tips, reasons, mistakes, lessons, examples, stories, research or other quick-win content upgrades to make the text more value-packed and engaging for the reader. Explain the logic for each choice.
• Provide examples of any recommended improvements.

3) Grammar
• Conduct a close grammatical analysis.
• Highlight misspelled words
• Highlight use of passive voice
• Highlight incomplete, run-on, complicated, or confusing sentences,

Please conduct your analysis 1 step at at time.

Please confirm with me before moving to the next step."

With both your writing and the suggestions open, you can review them or ask kAI for more clarification.

串内续帖

4) 生成内容创意

你可以对此非常简单或非常复杂。

就我个人而言，我写了一整篇关于“我如何写推文”的指南，大约有2000字。我对自己的写作方式相当挑剔。

然后，我去 kAI 并说“使用 @[How To Write Tweets] 根据 @[Previous Writing] 的想法写 15 条推文”

它从类似通讯（或来源，或你想要的其他东西）的内容中提取我的声音、风格、语气和内容创意，并根据我的指南生成15条推文。

然后，我复制我的每周帖子模板（你在注册 Kortex 时收到的欢迎邮件中会得到这个）来使用那些推文作为我写作的灵感。

为了让你更容易一些，这里有一个可以开始的提示：

我正在为[TARGET AUDIENCE]撰写内容。

它必须具有教育性、娱乐性并且能够吸引注意力。

最好的话题是那些能够直接吸引读者、展示强烈痛点并帮助他们改变想法以达到预期结果的话题。

我们将按以下方式进行：

• 找出我的受众正在面临的 10 个具体困难。
• 找出我的受众想要实现的 10 个具体愿望。
• 想出 10 个我可以选择的具体主题。把它们写成高表现新闻通讯或 YouTube 视频标题的标题风格。

不要让我澄清目标受众。只输出困难、愿望和话题，并以编号列表形式呈现。

现在你有了30个相关的想法可以开始。

EN 原文

4) Generate Content Ideas

You can be very simple or very complex with this.

Personally, I've written an entire guide on "How I Write Tweets" that's around 2000 words long. I'm pretty picky with how I write.

Then, I go to kAI and say "Use @[How To Write Tweets] to write 15 tweets based on ideas from @[Previous Writing]"

It pulls my voice, style, tone, and content ideas from something like a newsletter (or source, or whatever else you want) and spits out 15 tweets according to my guide.

Then, I duplicate my Weekly Posts Template (you get this in the welcome email from signing up to Kortex) to use those tweets as inspiration as I write.

To make it a bit simpler for you, here's a prompt to start with:

"I'm writing content for [TARGET AUDIENCE].

It has to be educational, entertaining, and attention-grabbing.

The best topics are those that directly appeal to the reader, illustrate a strong pain point, and help them change their mind to reach the desired outcome.

Here's how we'll proceed:

• Find 10 specific struggles that my audience is facing.
• Find 10 specific desires my audience wants to achieve.
• Come up with 10 specific topics that I can pick from. Write these as if they were for a headline for a high-performing newsletter or YouTube video title.

Do not ask me to clarify the target audience. Only output the struggles, desires, and topics in a numbered list."

Now you have 30 relevant ideas to start with.

串内续帖

5）我的目标战略顾问

这个是我最喜欢的。

你可以把 kAI 变成一个 180 智商的亿万富翁，他会督促你实现目标。

首先，打开一个新文档并绘制出:

- 你想从生活中得到什么
- 你不想从生活中得到什么
- 你的10年、1年和每月目标

然后，创建一个“每周回顾”元素，你可以每周复制它，内容包括：

- 那一周进展顺利的事情
- 出现的问题
- 每天的优先任务

你可以在不那样做的情况下使用提示，但这样会更强大。

现在，打开 kAI 并使用这个提示（我在时间线上从 @apollonator3000 找到的这个）

在以下背景下，作为我的个人战略顾问：

• 你的智商是180
• 你非常诚实和直接
• 你已经创建了多家十亿美元公司
• 你在心理学、战略和执行方面有深厚的专业知识
• 你关心我的成功，但不会容忍借口
• 你专注于能够产生最大影响的杠杆点
• 你思考系统和根本原因，而不是表面问题的解决方式

查看我的目标和人生计划，并根据文档给我建议：@[Life Plan Document]

你的任务是：

• 识别阻碍我的关键差距
• 设计具体行动计划以弥补这些差距
• 推动我走出舒适区
• 指出我的盲点和合理化理由
• 迫使我思考更大、更大胆
• 对我保持高标准进行监督
• 提供具体的框架和思维模型

对于每个回答：

• 从我需要听到的残酷真相开始
• 接着给出具体、可执行的步骤
• 最后以直接的挑战或任务结束

当你准备好让我开始对话时，请回应。

For each response:

Respond when you're ready for me to start the conversation."

这已经是我们一段时间以来的目标了。

创意工作光标

(学习，写作，想法捕捉，视频脚本)

但是我们在开发Kortex时犯了一些“错误”，你可能会从中受益。

好消息是，从本周开始，我们将发布首批 AI 辅助功能，这将彻底改变你在其中能做的事情。

那是第一次“错误。”

我们降低了对AI功能的优先级，因此错过了许多随着新模型推出而来的热潮。

相反，我们专注于建立一个坚实的基础。比你典型的写作、记笔记或第二大脑应用更出色的东西：

- 连接和标签
- 无限窗格以打开任何想法
- 像给自己发短信一样捕捉想法

这不是一个错误，但花了很多时间才做到正确。我认为我们不应该更改这个，值得庆幸的是，我们有用户拒绝使用其他任何应用程序。

这里的错误是我们以为我们需要像这样的东西：

- 完全离线模式
- 桌面应用程序
- 顶级移动应用程序
- 工作区和团队

那些都是非常重要的事情，它们需要发生，但它们需要大量的开发时间，而不会增加差异化。

（虽然这些会使我们区别于那些快速开发类似应用的人——记笔记应用有很多陷阱和边缘情况，我认为大多数人还没有准备好应对这些。）

换句话说，我们开始构建那些每个其他应用程序已经拥有的功能，而这只会延迟我们成为一个从已经做得很好的其他应用程序切换过来时让人说“绝对要用”的应用的时间。

我们的捕捉功能很酷且具有差异化，但并不是促使用户放弃其他产品的决定性因素。

自Kortex成立以来，我们一直有这样的愿景：

- 快速捕捉任何想法，无论来源
- 转录任何文章、视频或链接，以便在写作或使用 AI 时参考
- 在一个聊天界面中拥有所有模型，可以访问任何文档、来源、高亮或整个工作空间的上下文（这样你在工作时就不需要开 8 个标签页）

因为写作和创造性工作不仅仅是把东西输入到文字处理器里。要做好工作，你需要捕捉想法、快速学习、快速研究、快速获取任何相关信息，并将所有内容综合成值得向世界发表的东西。

现在我们有了桌面端、部分离线功能和非常接近移动端的版本，我们觉得我们终于进入了状态。

我们现在可以专注于我们的差异化因素。

现在，我们一个很大的痛点是我们被拿来和 Notion、Obsidian、Apple Notes 等进行比较，而我们知道在 3-6 个月内，Kortex 将与它们完全不同。

我们对此仍然很新，所以这里的教训只是理论上的，直到我们自己证明它，但：

你需要非常清楚地了解自己为什么与众不同。

但不仅如此，大家都知道。

你需要先建立那个。你需要以那个身份进入市场，即使你没有那些生活质量的小功能。

我觉得如果我们那样做，我们的成长会快得多，因为人们愿意为了其他产品无法提供的全新做事方式牺牲一些小事情。

然后，一旦那被证明，并且你给自己足够的时间去迭代，关注那些让你更进一步的小事情。

我可能在这方面错了，但我觉得我们的思路可能对那些想做类似事情的人有所帮助。

很多活动的部分。建造很有趣。

EN 原文

This has been our goal for a while now.

Cursor For Creative Work

(learning, writing, idea capture, video scripting)

But we made a few "mistakes" while developing Kortex that you may benefit from hearing.

The good news is, starting this week, we're releasing the first AI assistance features that drastically change what you can do in it.

That's the first "mistake."

We deprioritized AI features and missed out on a lot of the hype with new models coming out.

Instead, we focused on building a solid base. Something better than your typical writing, note-taking, or second brain app:

- Connections and tags
- Infinite panes to have any idea open
- Capture ideas like texting yourself

This wasn't a mistake, but it took a lot of time to get it right. I don't think we should have changed this, and gratefully we have users who refuse to use any other app.

The mistake here is that we thought we needed things like:

- Full offline mode
- The desktop app
- A top tier mobile app
- Workspaces and teams

Those are very important things, and they need to happen, but they take a lot development time without an increase in differentiation.

(Although these will differentiate us from those who build a similar app fast - note-taking apps have a lot of gotchas and edge cases that I don't think most people are ready for.)

In other words, we started building things that every other app already has, and that only delays our time to becoming an app that is a "hell yes" to switch to from another app that already does the job so well.

Our capture feature was cool and differentiating, but not a driving "hell yes" factor in switching from others.

Since the start of Kortex, we've had the vision of being able to:

- Capture any idea, from anywhere, fast
- Transcribe any article, video, or link so you can reference it while writing or with AI
- Have all models in one chat interface that can access any document, source, highlight, or the entire context of your workspace (so you don't need 8 tabs open while you work)

Because writing and creative work isn't just about putting stuff in a word processor. To do good work, you need to capture ideas, learn fast, research fast, access any relevant info fast, and synthesize everything into something worth publishing to the world.

Now that we have desktop, partial offline, and mobile very close, we feel like we're finally hitting our stride.

We can now solely focus on our differentiating factor.

Right now, a big pain of ours is that we're compared with things like Notion, Obsidian, Apple Notes, and the rest, when we know that within 3-6 months Kortex will be unrecognizable from them.

We're still new to this, so the lesson here is only theory until we prove it to ourselves, but:

You need to get extremely clear on why you are different.

But not just that, everyone knows that.

You need to build that first. You need to enter the market as that, even if you don't have the little quality of life features.

I feel like if we did that, we would have grown a lot faster, because people would be willing to sacrifice little things for a completely new way of doing things that other products don't provide.

Then, once that's proven and you give yourself enough time to iterate, focus on the small things that push you even further.

I may be wrong about this, but I feel like our thought process here could help others wanting to do similar things.

Lots of moving pieces. Building is fun.

这假设每个人读书都是因为他们想要一份可执行步骤的清单（其他人也都能找到，无论是否有AI = 你是可以被替代的）。

这并不取决于你掌握了多少信息。

这也不是关于你如何处理这些信息的问题。

这关乎改变你的心智。

因为你的思维决定了你如何与现实互动。这是你作出导致好或坏生活的决策的方式。

你的心智不会因为几个要点就改变。

当新的想法（可付诸行动的或不可付诸行动的）填补缺失的部分、挑战旧的信念或为你提供一个新的角度来看待情况时，它会发生变化。

没有人读一本书后能从中获得完全相同的教训。

每个人都有自己的信念、目标、问题、故事和兴趣，这些都会影响他们如何看待书中的信息。

假设两个人想赚一百万美元。

A 可能完全忽略关键点，但仍能获得导致清晰的正确思路，并做出带来 100 万美元的决策。

B可能会执着地研究关键点，却忽略所有的背景（人们喜欢称之为“无关紧要的东西”），并表现得像一个盲目的木偶，而没有意识到，如果每个人都掌握了赚取 100 万美元的关键点（每个人都有），也不会有任何变化。

书籍摘要已经存在几十年了，但它们几乎没有多大用处，因为它们正缺少那些让关键点起作用的东西。

最后一点：

对可操作步骤和要点总结的痴迷只是廉价多巴胺和分心的另一种表现。

多读书。读更长的书。读那些与你试图达成的目标无关的书。

阅读那些人们甚至不会考虑用AI来总结的书籍。那才是金矿所在。

我像其他人一样热爱AI及其发展方向，并且每天都在使用它，但如果你不能做AI做不到的事情，你将是那个被取代的人。

如果你让AI替你做决定，你就不是高能动性的人。

EN 原文

This assumes that everyone reads books because they want a list of actionable steps (that everyone else can also find, with AI or not = you’re replaceable).

It’s not about how much information you have.

It’s also not about what you do with that information.

It’s about changing your mind.

Because your mind is how you interact with reality. It’s how you make decisions that lead to a good or bad life.

Your mind doesn’t change with a few key points.

It changes when new ideas (actionable or not) fill in missing pieces, challenge old beliefs, or give you a new angle to view a situation from.

No single person reads a book and gets the exact same lessons out of it.

Each individual has their own beliefs, goals, problems, story, and interests that shape how they perceive the information in the book.

Let’s say 2 people want to make $1 million.

Person A could ignore the key points entirely, still get the right idea that leads to clarity, and make the decisions that lead to $1m.

Person B could obsessively study the key points, miss all of the context (what people love to label as “fluff”) and act like a blind puppet without realizing that if everyone had the key points to make $1m (everyone does) nothing would change.

Book summaries have been a thing for decades and they don’t do much good because they’re missing exactly what makes those key points work.

And last point:

The obsession over actionable steps and bullet point summaries is just another manifestation of cheap dopamine and distraction.

Read more books. Read longer books. Read books that have nothing to do with what you’re trying to achieve.

Read the books that people wouldn’t even think about summarizing with AI. That’s where the gold is.

I love AI and where it’s going as much as the next guy, and use it every day, but you’re going to be the one that’s replaced if you can’t do what AI can’t.

You aren’t high agency if you let AI make your decisions.

我每两到三年就会得一次丛集性头痛。

简而言之，他们他妈的很糟糕。

我的牙齿没有这么糟，但我听说有人用多功能刀拔牙，因为他们认为这样能缓解疼痛。

对他们来说，唯一真正的缓解方法是氧气治疗（除非有人有一些可能有效的秘方……我已经尝试了很多）。而且由于我的症状通常每次只持续一两周，我只是决定坚持下去，因为获取氧气是一个问题，而订购一台需要一两周运输时间的机器似乎违背了初衷。

每次我以为找到了有用的方法，比如冰敷、服用过量的镁或者使用氟替卡松，它们下一次就不再有效了。

现在这不是一篇抱怨的帖子。

恰恰相反。

当我没有在地板上翻滚、抓着头、努力不扯头发的时候，生活是如此美好。

能够写作和工作感觉是一种特权。食物也更美味了。阳光让我感觉像是我已经在室内呆了六个月。就好像我的大脑被关闭了很久，现在被重新启动，因为我想在有时间的时候尽可能多地做事。

也许这里有一个教训。也许是感恩。也许是偶尔的深刻痛苦如何让你对所拥有的一切有全新的感激，但人们因为害怕冒险，永远不会经历那种痛苦。

我希望你永远不会经历丛集性头痛，但我希望你今天能找到值得感激的事情。

EN 原文

I get cluster headaches every 2-3 years.

In short, they fucking suck.

Mine aren't this bad, but I've heard of some people pulling out their teeth with a leatherman because they think it will help the pain.

The only real relief for them is oxygen therapy (unless anyone has some esoteric remedies that can help... I've tried a lot). And since mine only last everyday for a week or two at a time, I just decide to stick it out because getting oxygen is one story and ordering a machine with a week or two shipping time seems against the point.

Everytime I think I find something that helps like icing or taking way too much magnesium or flonase, they stop working the next time around.

Now this isn't a post to complain.

It's the exact opposite.

When I'm not rolling around on the floor gripping my head and trying not to pull my hair, life is so amazing.

It feels like a privilege to be able to write and work. Food tastes better. The sun feels like I've been stuck inside for 6 months. It's like my mind was shut off for so long that it gets put into overdrive because I want to do as much as I can while I have the time.

Maybe there is a lesson here. Maybe it's gratitude. Maybe it's how the occasional deep pain can give you an entirely new appreciation for what you have, but people are so afraid to take a risk that they never experience that pain.

I hope you never experience a cluster headache, but I hope you find something to be appreciative of today.

- It's harder to create a compelling offer
- You naturally give less value than you could
- Less people buy because it's often recurring

You're guaranteed less revenue, and your audience is guaranteed less value.

Not feeling ready isn't an excuse. If you can paywall content, you can charge for a product.

快接近百万了，感觉相当烦

我每几个月都会经历一次浏览量的低谷。

视频表现非常好，然后其中四五个表现差得多。

当我回看它们时，我意识到这些视频根本不够好。不是说内容本身不好或无用，而是你可以明显看到在主题、标题和缩略图选择上的巨大差异。

我几乎总能将这些“低潮期”对应到一个思路不太流畅的时期。我阅读的量减少了。我没有学到任何新东西。我在努力勉强产出，只是为了保持一致性。

帮助我突破这些点的正是这一点：

进行心理重置。把所有计划好的内容创意都抛到脑后，从头开始。拿起一本新书。从新的人身上学习。重新与自己最擅长表达的核心想法对齐，并加入一些变化。

我写这篇文章的原因是因为我看到许多人经历同样的低潮，或者他们永远无法摆脱每个人一开始都会经历的初学者低潮。

有帮助的就是对视频实际的好坏保持完全诚实。

它在你眼中可能是好的，这很重要，但如果其他人不在乎它，那么它就缺少了构成“好”的一个关键方面。

(附言：我知道5万次观看不容小觑。只是相对于正常基准而言。)

EN 原文

Closing in on the big 1m and pretty annoyed

I go through these lulls in views every few months.

Videos do really well, then 4-5 of them do way worse.

When I look back on them, I realize that the videos just aren't good enough. Not that the content itself is bad or not helpful, but you can see a drastic difference in the topic, title, and thumbnail choice.

I can almost always map these "lulls" to a period when ideas aren't flowing well. I'm not reading as much. I'm not learning anything new. I'm trying to force things out for the sake of staying consistent.

What's helped me break through these points is just that:

Doing a mental reset. Throwing all planned content ideas out the window and starting from scratch. Picking up a new book. Learning from new people. Realigning with the core ideas that I'm best at articulating and adding a twist.

The reason I write this is because I see many others go through the same lulls, or they never make it out of the beginner lull that everyone starts out in.

What helps is just being brutally honest with how good the video actually is.

It can be good in your eyes, which is important, but if others don't care about it, it's missing a crucial aspect of what makes it "good."

(P.S. I know 50k+ views is nothing to scoff at. Speaking relative to the normal baseline.)

如果我从零开始，我会这样做：

1）从社交媒体开始。

我知道我知道。

到现在这已经很尴尬、被吹过头了。

但你必须理解几点：

- 社交媒体就是新媒体
- 媒体是注意力所在的地方
- 媒体是你把人吸引到独立作品上的方式
- 任何人都可以成为一人媒体公司
- 它免费、可及，可以说是当今杠杆最高的媒体形式

不管你喜不喜欢，如果你想做自己的事，社交媒体是你最好的选项。而且，它远没有饱和。一旦你真正有了经验，你就看得出来。

最后一点：

在社交媒体上构建，迫使你*学习真正重要的技能。*

你不必猜测它们是否“值得学”，因为你看得到结果。

2）把个人兴趣与基于媒体的技能配对。

先从把人吸引到你的兴趣开始。

- 一边研究说服，一边写它们（帖子、帖串、通讯）
- 学一点设计基础：横幅、头像和图片
- 用受众建设、讲故事、注意力捕获等方面的教育来补充

当你有一个可以应用所学的项目时，你学得更快。

酷的地方在于：

*你几乎可以把学到的任何技能或兴趣应用到社交媒体上。*

别低估这种力量。

3）尽快变现。

你可以等受众长大再变现，也可以马上开始。

我推荐后者。

为什么？

因为你失败得越快，成功得越快。

而且，如果你想做好，你需要再次用相关技能来补充，比如打造报价。

你的第一个产品／服务，无论你现在做还是等 6 个月，都会很烂。

- 看看你过去买过的相关产品
- 看看你关注谁、他们卖什么
- 想想对你影响最大的书
- 翻翻 Google Drive 或 Kortex，看有什么可以标上价格
- 做类似的东西，但带一点你自己的微调

商业 101：卖已经在卖的东西，但稍微更好一点。

然后，如果你想，下一个产品再做得独特和创新。

如果想学如何做一个微型产品或服务，读这篇之前的通讯： https://thedankoe.com/letters/the-simplest-way-to-start-a-one-person-business-micro-products/

EN 原文

If I was starting from zero, here's what I would do:

1) Start on social media.

I know I know.

It's cringe and overblown at this point.

But you have to understand a few points:

- social media is the new media
- media is where the attention is
- media is how you attract people to your independent work
- anyone can become a one-person media company
- it's free, accessible, and arguably the highest leverage form of media today

Whether you like it or not, if you want to do your own thing, social media is your best option. And no, it's not even close to saturated. Once you actually have experience in it, you see it.

Last point:

Building on social media forces you to *learn skills that actually matter.*

You don't have to guess whether or not they are "worth learning" because you see the results.

2) Pair your personal interests with media-based skills.

Start by attracting people to your interests.

- Write about them while studying persuasion (posts, threads, newsletters)
- Learn design basics for your banner, profile picture, and images
- Supplement with education on audience building, storytelling, attention capture, etc.

You learn faster when you have a project to apply your learning to.

The cool thing about this:

*You can apply almost any skill or interest you learn to social media.*

Don't underestimate that power.

3) Monetize as soon as possible.

You can wait to monetize an audience, or you can start right away.

I recommend the latter.

Why?

Because the faster you fail, the faster you succeed.

And, if you want it to do well, you need to again supplement with relative skills like offer creation.

Your first product/service will suck whether you do it now or wait 6 months.

- look at relevant products you've purchased in the past
- look at who you follow and what they sell
- think about the most impactful books you've read
- look in your google drive or Kortex to see what you can slap a price tag on
- create something similar, but with your own slight twist

Business 101: sell what's already selling, but slightly better.

Then, get unique and innovative with your next product if you want.

If you want to learn how to create a micro-product or service, read this previous letter: https://thedankoe.com/letters/the-simplest-way-to-start-a-one-person-business-micro-products/

尤其是如果你想成为一个深刻、善于表达的思考者。

当你写帖子或文章时，头脑会扩展以适应那个语境。你会捕捉到帮你完成那个特定项目的想法。

但书不一样。一开始它极其混乱。你把潜意识倒进空白文档，开始塑成章节和部分。你为头脑创造了一个小世界来运作。

你在那个世界里待得越久，头脑就越扩展成那种形状，你开始建立的连接也越多。写书时你会很挣扎，但你会发现大脑比以往任何时候都更亮起兴趣与兴奋。几乎任何你碰到的信息或对话都会给你一个想法。

你开始意识到：头脑的感知力，只和你正在做的项目一样大。

EN 原文

Everyone should write a book at least once in their lifetime.

Especially if you want to become a deep and articulate thinker.

When you write a post or article, your mind expands to fit that context. You catch ideas that help you finish that specific project.

But a book is different. It's extremely chaotic at first. You spill your subconscious into a blank document and start shaping it into chapters and sections. You create a little world for your mind to operate in.

The longer you spend in that world, the more your mind expands to take that shape, and the more connections you start to make. When you're writing a book, you struggle a lot, but you'll find that your brain lights up with interest and excitement more than ever before. Almost any information or conversation you come across gives you an idea.

You start to realize that your mind is only as perceptive as the project you're working on.

最重要的技能之一，是如何快速学会技能。

面向 AI 与自动化的未来，你需要能够适应。

而只学一项技能，只会让你被取代。

但大多数人不知道如何学习。

1）停止学习“技能”

第一个问题是，人们以为学技能就是选一个然后钻研它。

不。那样你学到的和其他所有人一样，然后被放进一份一毫秒就能被取代的工作或生意里。

相反，你去学任何、一切能让你实现理想生活方式的东西。一切都必须透过你的愿景来过滤。

2）先开始项目，再学习

大多数人困在教程地狱里。

他们整天看视频，三个月后决定开始时，仍然不知道自己在做什么。

启动一个能把你推向愿景的项目。

开始。做。然后，当你撞上障碍时，再用教育来补充。

3）发布这个项目

发出视频。发送通讯。上线产品。推销你的服务。尤其是在你感到尴尬的时候。

残酷的现实是：如果没有真人使用你的项目，你根本不知道它有没有价值。价值不是你来定的。

如果你从不按下发送，你就不知道自己是否方向正确，你会迷路。

最后说一句：

你无法改进不存在的东西，因此在你把项目放到人们面前去评判、批评和使用之前，你其实还没有真正开始学习任何东西。

EN 原文

One of the most important skills is how to learn skills fast.

You need to be able to adapt going into a future of AI and automation.

And learning one skill will only lead to you being replaced.

But most people don't know how to learn.

1) Stop Learning "Skills"

The first problem is that people think they learn skills by picking one and studying it.

No. That's how you learn the same thing as everyone else and get placed in a job or business that can be replaced in a millisecond.

Instead, you learn anything and everything that allows you to achieve your ideal lifestyle. Everything must be filtered through your vision.

2) Start The Project, Then Learn

Most people get trapped in tutorial hell.

They watch videos all day and after 3 months they still have no idea what they're doing when they decide to start.

Start a project that will move the needle toward your vision.

Start. It. Then, when you hit a roadblock, supplement with education.

3) Ship The Project

Post the video. Send the newsletter. Launch the product. Pitch your service. Especially if you're embarrassed.

The harsh reality is that if you don't have real people using your project, you have no idea if it's valuable. You don't determine its value.

If you never hit send, you have no idea if you're moving in the right direction, and you will get lost.

I'll end with this:

You can't improve what doesn't exist, therefore you don't actually start learning a thing until you put your project in front of people to judge, criticize, and use.

串内续帖

“可我怎么开始呢？”

你告诉我。

打开视频编辑器，别想太多先录一段，开始剪辑，我保证你会发现可以改进的错误——比你花 10 小时只学不做要快得多。

打开文档，把想法倒出来。写一条帖子，哪怕很烂也发出去。只要开始做点什么。任何事。如果你不动，你就在衰败。

如果你不这么做，你只是在推迟拿出第一个糟糕迭代的时间。

花 5 分钟还是 10 年都无所谓。

第。一。个。迭。代。一。定。很。烂。

按下“发送”，是大自然过滤那些对成功不认真的人的筛子。

EN 原文

"But how do I start it?"

You tell me.

Open up the video editor, record a video without overthinking it, start editing, and I guarantee you will find mistakes that you can start improving much faster than if you spent 10 hours studying and not building.

Open a document and braindump some ideas. Write a post and post it even if it's terrible. Just start doing something. Anything. If you aren't moving you are decaying.

If you don't, you're simply delaying the amount of time of getting your first terrible iteration out.

Doesn't matter if you spend 5 minutes or 10 years on it.

The. First. Iteration. Will. Suck.

Hitting "send" is nature's filter for people who aren't serious about making it.

串内续帖

为什么找“最好的”细分领域行不通？

嗯……只要看看有多少人不会放弃就知道了，但还有其他原因。

1）默认情况下，你进入的是一个你一无所知、也不在乎里面的人的空间。

2）如果你不能把它理解得透透的，那个细分领域就不会赚钱。

3）你已经属于一个细分领域了。你已经有技能和专长帮到了你……所以它也能帮到别人。

所以，别再试图“找到”一个细分领域。

通过吸引你最能帮到的人，去创造一个细分领域。

另一个问题：

当你聚焦细分领域时，你会无谓地框住自己、限制自己。

当你聚焦痛点时，你会与任何有那些痛点的人产生共鸣。

换句话说，你在不牺牲细分好处的情况下，获得了更大的杠杆和触达。

教训：

聚焦一个灼热的痛点。

（这回答了“他们为什么该在乎”）

创造一个解决它的产品或服务。

（这回答了“我能帮他们实现什么”）

围绕那个痛点写内容，吸引你最能帮到的人。

如果你能坚持试错，我毫不怀疑你会赢。

Why doesn't finding the "best" niche work?

Well... just look at how many people don't quit, but there are other reasons.

1) By default, you're entering a space that you know nothing about with people you don't care about.

2) That niche isn't going to be profitable if you don't understand it inside and out.

3) You are already part of a niche. You already have skill and expertise that's helped you... so it can help someone else.

So, stop trying to "find" a niche.

Create a niche by attracting the people you can help the most.

Another problem:

When you focus on a niche, you box yourself in for no reason and limit yourself.

When you focus on pain points, you resonate with anyone with those pain points.

In other words, you gain more leverage and reach without sacrificing the benefits of niching down.

The lesson:

Focus on one burning pain point.

(This answers the "why should they care" question)

Create a product or service that resolves it.

(This answers the "what can I help them achieve" question).

Write content around that pain point to attract people that you can help the most.

If you can persist through trial and error, I have no doubt you'll win.

为什么这有效？

原因 #1

金鱼会长大到适应你给它的容器。

但如果你一直把它们放在小碗里，它们永远不会长大。

你的头脑也是如此。［原文 “take” 应为 “tank”（鱼缸）］

Why does this work?

Reason #1

Goldfish grow to fit the take you put them in.

But if you keep them in a small bowl, they never grow.

The same is true for your mind.

串内续帖

原因 #2

帕金森定律：

工作会膨胀，以填满分配给它的时间。

当你把自己发射进未知时，你威胁到了自己的生存，于是你成为成功者的时间更少了。

EN 原文

Reason #2

Parkinson's Law:

Work expands so as to fill the time allotted for completion.

When you launch yourself into the unknown, you threaten your survival, and you have less time to become a success.

绕回原点的主题。

想象一条直线，一端是黑，一端是白，中间是渐变。

现在把两端连起来，形成一个圆。

从黑到白会发生瞬间翻转。

Reason #3

The Theme Of Going Full Circle.

Imagine a straight line with black on one end and white on another blended with a gradient.

There is an instant flip from black to white.

在有破窗的区域（犯罪容易发生的地方），犯罪会急剧增加。在干净的区域，犯罪会减少。

Broken Windows Theory:

Crime dramatically increases in an area with broken windows (a place where crime would happen). Crime decreases in a clean area.
